Throughout my career, I worked closely with children and families, gaining a deep understanding of the emotional, social, and developmental foundations that support healthy family life. ​ After becoming a mother myself, my perspective shifted in a profound way. I began to recognise a pattern I had seen repeatedly in both education and family settings: parents so often place their own wellbeing last while prioritising their children’s needs. Over time, this imbalance can lead to emotional exhaustion, overwhelm, and burnout, and when parents struggle, children inevitably feel the impact too. Families can find themselves stuck in a cycle of simply surviving, rather than truly thriving. ​ This realisation led me to create Wellbeing Mumma. I wanted to support families in restoring balance, connection, and emotional safety within their homes. My work is grounded in evidence-based research, family psychology, and practical wellbeing strategies that fit realistically into everyday family life. I offer gentle guidance, simple tools, and compassionate support to help both adults and children feel calmer, more regulated, and more connected. ​ ​ At the heart of my approach is the belief that family wellbeing is interconnected.
